newsitem.title: TURKEY: Procedure for MPs' approval of Turkish coalition.
newsitem.headline: Procedure for MPs' approval of Turkish coalition.

text.p: Here is the procedure for the approval by parliament of Turkey's new anti-Islamist coalition, endorsed on Monday by President Suleyman Demirel:

Secularist Mesut Yilmaz officially became the new prime minister when Demirel approved his cabinet list. He will physically take over the job from Islamist Necmettin Erbakan at a handing-over ceremony later on Monday.
Yilmaz or one of his cabinet members must read out the government's programme in parliament and officially apply for a confidence vote by next Monday.
Deputies will debate the government's newly announced policies two days after they are read out in parliament, and then break for another full day before the confidence vote is held.
The constitution does not specify how the vote should be carried out but the speaker's office says the government needs a majority of the votes cast in the 550-seat chamber.
Two parliamentary seats are empty and the speaker, a member of Yilmaz's Motherland Party, cannot vote.
If the coalition lost the confidence vote, the president would have to ask another leader to form a government. That would probably spark weeks of political horse-trading between the parties.
Conservative rival Tansu Ciller is reckoned to be next in line for the job if Yilmaz fails.
Yilmaz's left-right alliance is a minority coalition of three parties that is supported by a fourth parliamentary grouping.
